text:
Maria: Heads-up — Enterprise prospect 'Zenith Health' sent a hard ask: 99.99% uptime + p95 < 100ms for embeddings. Sales says they'll sign if engineering can commit, need confirmation by EOD.
Devon: Thanks. Do we have recent p95 numbers for embeddings-prod and any caveats?
Sasha: p95 ~85ms in us-east with current caching and vector index. 99.99% uptime is doable only with dedicated capacity + multi-region failover; hosted best-effort won't guarantee that.
Alan: Can you paste the exact contract language? Need to check month window and credit terms.
Maria: From the customer: "Provider will maintain 99.99% monthly uptime; service credits apply for breaches. Maintenance with 48h notice excluded. Customer requires 24/7 priority support and escalation to on-call within 30min for sev1s."
Devon: That support ask bumps this into our premium S-level. Product: how do we want to route — backlog feature work vs capacity purchase? Seems like Dedicated + VPC is likely.
Sasha: Agreed. For hosted, risk of violating SLO is non-trivial under traffic spikes. Recommend a hybrid: reserved dedicated pool for their critical endpoints plus automated failover to a warmed standby in another region.
Chris: From SRE: We can meet 99.99 for a dedicated offering if they commit to a reserved capacity contract. Provisioning + full failover test will need ~8 weeks and an expanded on-call rota.
Maria: Sales needs a crisp proposal: acceptance criteria, timeline, and delta cost for the customer. Product — can you draft the SLO proposal and negotiation bullets?
Alan: I'll take product lead. Initial checklist I'll include: 1) SLO definition and measurement window (monthly), 2) Maintenance and force majeure exclusions, 3) Support tier and RTO/RPO, 4) Required infra (dedicated capacity, multi-region), 5) Rollout plan and gating tests.
Sasha: Add launch acceptance tests: automated failover smoke, latency regression threshold (+10% vs baseline), and a small eval prompt set for quality monitoring post-cutover.
Devon: Also define fallback policy: automatic model-variant fallback, prefix caching, and rate-limiting thresholds to prevent cascade during degraded states.
Alan: Assigning: @Sasha + @Alan to draft the SLO and rollout plan by tomorrow 11:00 PT. @Devon to validate infra assumptions and cost. @Maria to align sales messaging with the customer.
km-bot: Reminder: create support-case-template tag: customer:zenith, sla:99.99, product:embeddings, priority:premium.
Maria: One more — customer insists on escalation to an SRE within 30 minutes for sev1. Is that something we can guarantee?
Chris: 30 minutes is aggressive but possible with premium support add-on and expanded on-call coverage. We'll include cost and headcount impact in the proposal.
Alan: Noted. We'll include runbooks, on-call escalation matrix, and estimated ops cost. Draft will go into #product tomorrow for review.
Maria: Sales will pause active push until we have the proposal. Please flag any blockers early.
Sasha: tl;dr: recommend offering Dedicated + multi-region failover, 8-week provisioning runway, premium support add-on for 30min escalation, launch criteria (smoke failover + latency guardrails), and monitoring/eval plan. I'll include mitigations to limit cost.
Devon: +1. If product signs off, I'll break down engineering tasks and a tentative sprint plan (2 epics: infra + runbook/monitoring).
Maria: Thanks everyone — closing this thread for now, will reopen after the proposal. :thumbsup:
